argument: The statement contains no resistance-carrying quantity (charge is fixed as a co-creating partner, not resistance) and no separation made by distance: the matter/antimatter difference is an inexact symmetry, and the rule says symmetries keep their shape. No resistance-caused cost or distance-made separation is actually present, so no rule-compliant turn exists.

This is a symmetry, and the rule says symmetries keep their shape; the forcing of the gauge fields into existence is a requirement, not a cost caused by resistance, and no quantity in the statement carries resistance. No rule-compliant turn exists.

Mass m carries resistance, but in this statement the resistance is the result of the coupling, not the cause of any cost or limit: the formula hands mass out, it does not charge anything to resistance, and the Yukawa coupling is itself undetermined by R. With no resistance-caused cost and no distance-made separation present, the equation keeps its shape.

This is an identity backed by conservation laws, both of which the rule says keep their shape; energy, momentum and charge are all fixed in advance as non-resistance quantities. No cost caused by resistance and no separation made by distance appears, so no rule-compliant turn exists.

Running couplings and energy are both fixed as non-resistance quantities, and the growing of one coupling and the falling of the other are changes with scale, not costs caused by resistance or separations made by distance. No rule-compliant turn exists.

The many-orders-of-magnitude difference is a separation between two estimates, but nothing in the statement makes that separation by distance, and vacuum energy density is fixed as energy, which does not carry resistance. A definition keeps its shape, so no rule-compliant turn exists.

This is an identity of exclusivity, which keeps its shape; the coupling constant is fixed as interaction strength, not opposition, and the statement contains no cost or limit caused by resistance and no separation made by distance. No rule-compliant turn exists.

The relation is an identity, which the rule says keeps its shape, and energy is the one E shared by both sides of the mirror, so the mass term's contribution to E is not a cost caused by resistance; mass here is carried, not charged. No distance-made separation appears either, so no rule-compliant turn exists.

This is an identity equating a quantity with itself, which keeps its shape; both sides of the equality are the same resistance-carrying mass, and the statement charges no cost to resistance and separates nothing by distance (the freely falling observer feels no gravity at all). No rule-compliant turn exists.

The interval is zero: no distance is present to make a separation, and the vanishing identity keeps its shape; the speed of light is fixed in advance as the limit, not an opposition, so nothing in the statement is caused by resistance. No rule-compliant turn exists.

The statement itself says only the relative velocity matters, and velocity and frequency are both fixed as non-resistance quantities; the lowered rate on recession with a raised rate on approach is exactly the relationship kept under a flipped condition, which is the keeps reading, not a turn. No resistance-caused cost or distance-made separation is actually present.

The never-exceeds-c limit is fixed in advance as the limit, not an opposition: a limit caused by resistance would turn around, but this one is caused by the composition identity itself, which keeps its shape, and velocities carry no resistance. No rule-compliant turn exists.
